# Decision catalog (auto-generated)

Read first. Then read `decisions/<slug>.md` for the full body. Refreshed by sprint execution when a sprint's corpus deltas touch `decisions/`. Do not edit by hand — changes will be overwritten.

## Decisions

- `acquire-prefix-fallback` — Policy lookup for acquisition failures falls back from the exact producer-declared class to the `acquire/*` family before the unknown-class default; the fallback is documented at the lookup site (see `concept:error-policy`).
- `acquire-unavailable-carveout` — Five acquire-phase error handlers — unavailable, producer error, nil frame id, fan-out substitution failure, and lock-spec substitution failure — remain explicitly named carve-outs outside the unified claim-handle resolution engine, sharing one downstream policy-application path; unavailable and producer error fall back to the synthetic classes `acquire/unavailable` and `acquire/producer_error`, and the other three route by their own synthetic class alone.
- `advisory-locks` — Postgres advisory locks + sqlite equivalent at session level.
- `allowlist-defaults-open` — A bundled service's reference allowlist defaults open: with the operator env var unset the service accepts every name the template declares; a set-but-empty allowlist is an explicit closed boundary; a destination allowlist defaults the other way.
- `artifact-layout` — A per-run directory under a stable per-root parent, named by timestamp plus run name, holding the run's state database; the database stays openable with widely available tooling — no rimsky-specific reader.
- `artifact-root-discovery` — From the current working directory, walk parent directories for the first existing rimsky workdir marker. Create one in the current working directory if none is found.
- `asset-materialize-endpoint-retired` — The control surface exposes no asset-materialize verb; re-materialization is expressed through messages — the empty-message whole-instance re-run or an author-designed typed message via subscription edges.
- `async-callback-outcome-oneof` — Oneof `success` | `error` | `park`; exactly one outcome key.
- `async-callback-persistent-registry` — Async-callback registration persists on the dispatch row itself, written in the same transaction as the dispatch-state mutation; the callback handler resolves a callback to its dispatch by acknowledgement id.
- `async-callback-post-json` — HTTP POST with a JSON outcome body to the supervisor's async-callback endpoint, keyed by the async-acknowledgement identifier on the route path (see `concept:supervisor`).
- `attribute-bytes-in-the-row` — An attribute bag and a node-run's scratch are stored whole in a byte column of their own row and commit in the row's transaction; the database engine's per-value cap is the only ceiling, and rimsky spills nothing to a store outside the row.
- `attribute-carry-forward` — On each dispatch the runtime hydrates the attribute bag from the most-recent prior node-run of the same node in the same RunScope, then overlays per-field source-substitution for source-bound properties; first dispatch falls back to schema defaults.
- `attribute-set-as-body` — A message-sender node's `attributes:` block is the message body.
- `auth-anonymous-via-empty-key-ledger` — Rely on the existing `concept:anonymous-mode` behavior for loopback admission: a fresh per-run sqlite database has zero rows in the API-key ledger, so every request is admitted as a synthetic admin identity.
- `auth-api-key-bearer` — Api-key as bearer token.
- `auth-audit-log-verbatim-bodies` — An auth audit-log row stores the request body verbatim; rimsky redacts nothing and truncates nothing (see `concept:event-log`, `concept:inertness`).
- `auth-dry-run-mode-floor-on-key` — A grant whose mode is dry-run pins the key to dry-run regardless of request flag.
- `auth-dry-run-request-flag` — A per-request dry-run flag on writes.
- `auth-grant-scope` — A per-grant scope map of action-specific dimension keys (e.g., template tag) constraining the action (see `concept:permission`).
- `blessed-invariant-annotations` — A load-bearing safety property is recorded in the decision or story that owns it, proven by a test, and cited from code by the ordinary annotation; there is no dedicated invariant tag and no numbered catalog.
- `breakpoint-matcher-executor-scope-permissive` — A breakpoint matcher validates an executor key against every executor the deployment declares, not only against the executors the target template dispatches to (see `concept:breakpoint`).
- `build-cgo-disabled` — CGO disabled for all builds.
- `build-tool-makefile` — A Makefile at the repo root is the single source of truth for build orchestration (builds, tests, lint, images, release chain).
- `bundled-executor-inproc-capability-advertisement` — Bundled in-proc handlers advertise capabilities into the discovery cache at registration time from the same package-scope accessors that feed the gRPC observability handshake; the periodic re-probe loop skips these static entries.
- `bundled-recipes-production-paths` — A recipe induces the behavior it demonstrates through production paths, never a synthetic probe or a test hook; the release run generates the recipes from the tree and places them in the release documentation.
- `bundled-registry-entrypoint` — A single bundled registration entrypoint constructs and registers every bundled service handler across the in-proc executor and claim-producer registries; bundled registrations never shadow an operator-configured endpoint of the same name.
- `byte-equal-conflict-default` — Rimsky compares claim scopes by byte equality to decide whether two claims conflict; a producer advertising the scopes-conflict capability supplies its own overlap predicate instead (see `concept:claim-scope`).
- `cascade-flags-on-subscribes` — Cascade-behavior flags (currently `force_upstream_refresh`) are fields of the subscription-entry shape, not of the substitution-ref shape and not of a separate block.
- `cascade-flags-required-no-defaults` — `force_upstream_refresh` is a required field on every subscription entry; registration rejects entries missing it.
- `cascade-inside-settlement` — The parent-settlement cascade bridge fires within the settle-children primitive, not alongside it at call sites (see `concept:child-execution`).
- `child-execution-naming` — The primitive pair is named dispatch-children / settle-children.
- `claim-producer-vocabulary-boundary` — The store→claim-producer rename covers every shipped user-facing surface; internal test machinery and the per-producer storage-layer "store" sense are exempt by design.
- `claimant-guard-helper` — Each persistence driver (Postgres, SQLite) routes its claimant-guarded mutations through one internal helper that appends the guard predicate; no hand-written copies of the predicate exist outside the helper (see `concept:claim-handle`).
- `claude-agent-cli-expose-env-field` — Claude-agent node config carries a per-node expose-env field intersected against the operator allowlist; there is no container-wide exposure knob.
- `claude-agent-cli-mcp-servers-inline-only` — Per-node MCP servers are declared inline only, across three transports (http, stdio, module — with `http-loopback` an alias for module); no named-reference shape, no operator-side catalog.
- `claude-agent-env-passthrough-allowlist` — claude-agent exposes executor-container env to the CLI child only through the intersection of an operator allowlist and a per-node expose-env list; rimsky's own substitution grammar never carries the secret.
- `claude-agent-error-classes-closed` — The bundled claude-agent executor's declared error classes are a closed set: advertised in full through its observability surface, with emission of any undeclared class rejected at the executor's own boundary; member spellings live in the declaration and its tests, not the corpus.
- `claude-agent-session-attribute` — claude-agent's CLI session token is a carry-forward attribute riding the attribute delta on Success and the Park scratch slot on Park; dispatch reads scratch first with attribute fallback, continuity intra-frame only.
- `cli-spawn-mechanism` — claude-agent spawns the `claude` binary as a direct child via the Go standard-library subprocess mechanism, with no intermediate runtime layer.
- `cli-verb` — The ephemeral-run capability is exposed as a sub-verb under the compose dispatcher, sibling to the existing compose lifecycle verbs (up, down, plan, status).
- `coding-style` — Rimsky's coding methodology is Plumbline, consumed as a Claude Code plugin.
- `comment-hygiene-uniform-rule` — Comment-hygiene violations are resolved by tag-or-delete on a per-site basis.
- `compose-driver-sends-empty-message-after-create` — The compose driver sends an empty message per declared instance after creating it, via the same HTTP client path it already uses for instance-create, with a deterministic idempotency key derived from the instance key.
- `compose-engine-reuse` — Reuse the existing compose engine that the `up`/`down`/`plan`/`status` verbs already use.
- `config-enforced-fitness-tests` — A decision enforced solely by a configuration surface is linked to code through a grouped fitness test per enforcement surface carrying the `@decision:` annotations; citation tags are never stamped into configs.
- `config-format-yaml` — YAML is the single configuration format for the unified config file and per-service configs.
- `config-yaml-loading-policy` — Every loader of `rimsky.yml` (root loader, sibling-block re-reads, service-side opts loaders) uses one shared implementation with strict env-expansion (`${VAR}`-only, unset is a load-time hard error) and strict YAML decoding (`KnownFields(true)`, unknown keys rejected).
- `conformance-suite-per-protocol` — One conformance suite per protocol under the protocols module's conformance package, exposed as a per-protocol conformance subcommand on the CLI.
- `coverage-wildcard-asymmetry` — A wildcard `attribute/*` subscription covers both per-field and whole-pull reads of the same sender; a per-field subscription covers only the matching per-field read and does not cover a whole-pull read.
- `cron-robfig-v3` — Cron expressions are parsed by robfig/cron/v3, pinned to that major line.
- `debug-channel-gate-paused-or-breakpoint` — The control-API debug-override endpoint is legal iff the instance is paused (the existing instance-level pause flag is true) OR the instance holds at least one unresumed pause-mode breakpoint hit blocking a runner.
- `default-port-allocation` — Shipped default listening ports come from two reserved blocks: 8080-8099 for rimsky's core listeners and 9000-9199 for the bundled services; no two shipped defaults coincide, a listener with no built-in default takes its port from the operator, and a fitness check enumerates every shipped default.
- `depguard-consumption-isolation` — The protocols module only; not the foundation module, graph layer, runtime layer, or control layer.
- `depguard-foundation-internal` — External imports of the foundation module's internal package are forbidden.
- `depguard-foundation-purity` — Stdlib + the protocols module + chosen libs only; no graph, runtime, or control layer imports.
- `depguard-graph-purity` — The graph layer's import surface is unconditionally pure: the dependency lint denies runtime, control, and cmd imports with no per-site exemptions, and the runtime layer's tick loop calls step functions the graph layer exports.
- `depguard-pgx-isolation` — Only the foundation module's postgres persistence driver, the services module, the cmd group, the test-support package, and the scenario harness in the test group.
- `depguard-protocols-purity` — Stdlib plus the official gRPC and protobuf libraries, the chosen UUID library, and the chosen YAML library only.
- `depguard-runtime-purity` — The foundation module + the graph layer + the protocols module; not the control layer.
- `deposit-detection-watermark` — deposit detection is periodic listing against a durable watermark; at-least-once publish with idempotency keys.
- `deposit-settle-window` — optional per-watch mtime-quiescence window holds still-changing deposits out of discovery; sensor-layer, default off.
- `design-link-annotations` — Source-code annotations linking sites to their concept, story, or decision slug at the point of enforcement.
- `destination-allowlists-default-closed` — A bundled service's destination allowlist defaults closed: with the operator env var unset the service blocks every loopback, private, unique-local, link-local, multicast and unspecified address, and admits only the http and https schemes; an operator opens a range by naming it as a CIDR or a bare address.
- `doc-accuracy-gates` — Documentation that enumerates code facts is kept honest by build-time gates mechanically diffing the prose against those facts (the after-code-changes rules gate and the substitution-doc gate); new enumerating doc surfaces follow the pattern.
- `doc-residue-reshape-pass` — Doc-residue comment-hygiene violations resolve under a reshape-first per-site rule: doc-position comments in marker-carrying files reshape into GoDoc/JSDoc form; everything else resolves per `decision:comment-hygiene-uniform-rule`.
- `emit-work-completed` — The terminal-application step appends a work-completed event carrying the same identifiers as its work-started twin plus the terminal kind (see `story:work-completed-emitted`, `concept:event-log`).
- `empty-message-as-root-trigger` — Every template's declared-types set carries an implicit empty-string type-path entry, seeded at registration.
- `enroll-token-is-api-key` — The enrollment credential is not a new token type: it reduces to an api-key carrying an enrollment permission, exchanged at the control API's enrollment surface for a short-lived certificate identity (see `concept:service-auth`).
- `entry-absorption-flag` — Delegation's entry absorption is an entry-absorbed boolean carried on the dispatch-children primitive's input, not a pre-step before dispatch (see `concept:child-execution`).
- `env-as-substitution-source-kind` — Host-environment variables ride the substitution grammar as a sixth source kind, `env.<VAR_NAME>`, resolved at dispatch time from the supervisor process's environment.
- `env-var-convention-across-modes` — Each bundled service handler reads its own operator config from the same env-var names in both containerized and all-in-one mode; rimsky.yml carries no per-service config content.
- `env-var-registry` — Every `RIMSKY_*` environment variable read by live code appears in a generated registry table backed by a fitness test, and endpoint variables name their target service.
- `envelope-type-discriminator` — The message envelope's discriminator field is `type` and carries the message type-path; the publisher-subscription counterpart is `message_type`, with no separate kind vocabulary.
- `event-log-kind-enum` — The canonical set of operational event-kind values is a closed enum at the protocol layer, rimsky's app logic consumes typed values only, and every declared kind has at least one emit site (see `concept:event-log`).
- `event-log-payload-shapes` — Typed oneof payloads for a settled subset of operational event kinds (state-transition, work-started, lock-acquired, claim-acquired, and the rest of the oneof's members); free-form JSON payload for signal-class events and for every operational kind outside the typed subset (see `concept:event-log`).
- `executor-unary-rpc` — `rpc Execute(ExecuteRequest) returns (Outcome)` — unary.
- `exit-codes` — Zero for all-instances-success; one for at-least-one-failure (including park-timeout as a failure); two for the run-timeout exceeded; the conventional interrupt-signal exit code (signal number 2 plus 128) for interrupt during shutdown.
- `expected-attributes-schema-closed` — The expected-attributes schema an executor advertises declares every node-attribute key the executor reads and admits no other; registration rejects a node carrying an undeclared key (see `concept:observability`, `concept:executor`).
- `exposure-no-config` — One-shot (embedded-stack) mode is exposed only through its dedicated CLI verb; no operator-facing config knob selects it.
- `fan-out-and-delegation-are-distinct-mechanisms` — Fan-out and sub-graph delegation are documented and implemented as two distinct mechanisms sharing only a thin dispatch helper; settlement is intentionally split because their fan-in shapes differ (see `concept:fan-out`, `concept:delegation`, `concept:child-execution`).
- `fanout-attribute-merge-rejected` — Per-partition executor attribute writebacks never aggregate onto the fan-out parent's attribute bag; an author who needs per-fan-out aggregation routes it through the claim-producer protocol (see `concept:fan-out`).
- `fanout-list-array-store-agnostic` — The list partition grammar for fan-out is store-agnostic: both bundled claim producers serve it through the same split-scope surface; which store holds the parent claim is a deployment choice, not a separate capability.
- `fanout-parallelism-cap-per-process` — A fan-out's parallelism cap is an in-process semaphore bounding how many clones one supervisor process dispatches concurrently, enforced once per process rather than pooled across the cluster (see `concept:fan-out`).
- `fold-ownership-bail` — The verify-before-run ownership-bail path resolves through the unified claim-handle resolution engine as its own source kind; no caller-owned per-claim Abandon plus claimant-guarded delete exists outside the engine for this path (see `concept:terminal-resolution`).
- `force-upstream-refresh-via-receiver-keyed-map` — A receiver-keyed map of upstream node-types is built at registration from every `subscribes:` entry carrying `force_upstream_refresh: true`.
- `frame-isolation-is-structural` — Frame isolation is a structural, load-bearing invariant of rimsky: no state ever crosses a frame boundary through any channel other than a message envelope on the instance's queue. Not tunable, not per-node opt-in-able, not per-signal exception-able. Every runtime surface — substitution, gates, cascade-mode, diff-gate, wait-set, cascade-walker, operator actions — is intra-frame by construction. Multi-frame workflows carry state through messages; convergence is queue-empty.
- `graceful-shutdown` — Shutdown is polite-then-forceful: stop new dispatches, politely terminate in-flight work and spawned children, then stop waiting when the hardcoded grace expires — five seconds where the CLI supervises children it spawned, ten seconds where a bundled service drains its own serving surfaces, thirty seconds on the deployed core paths — the container entrypoint, the standalone role processes, the host-daemon proxy's listeners, and the supervisor's dispatch drain; every path escalates a second interrupt to immediate hard exit through one shared helper, and the host daemon's wait for a spawned child is the one operator-tunable window.
- `grpc-google-official` — The official upstream gRPC and protobuf libraries for Go.
- `grpc-internal-protocols` — gRPC for the declared service protocols, with three named HTTP-JSON exceptions: the supervisor's HTTP executor transport, the bundled executor's HTTP bridge, and the executor-to-supervisor callback, keepalive, and attribute-writeback routes.
- `guard-conformance-suite` — The driver-parity suite (the cross-driver test library run against both persistence drivers) carries a guard suite: for every mutating claim-handle and node-run ownership operation, acting as the wrong supervisor must change nothing — asserted identically against both drivers.
- `handler-package-in-service-directory` — A bundled service with both a standalone and an in-process surface exposes its handler code as importable Go packages alongside a thin standalone `main`, so both modes run the same handler code; a single-surface service owes a standalone command and nothing more.
- `hard-dep-field-no-special-case` — The cascade walker and edge builder do not read any attribute-field `hard_dep:` flag.
- `hard-dep-settled-guard` — The upstream-refresh pull carries a settled-this-frame guard: an already-settled upstream is not re-affirmed on receiver re-visits, protecting frame termination without weakening the multi-hard-dep rendezvous.
- `held-as-state-not-phase` — `held` is promoted from a node-run lifecycle phase to a first-class state in the seven-state machine, with cascade walks deferred to the auto-terminal handler so downstream sees only committed/abandoned signals, never provisional ones.
- `held-claim-poison-propagation` — A held claim's aggregate outcome resolves to Abandon the moment any holder fails, and every still-active holder settles failed under the abandoned error class (see `concept:claim-handle`, `concept:auto-terminal`).
- `host-daemon-late-bind-schema-check-deferred` — Rimsky checks a late-bound executor's attribute-schema conformance at each dispatch, after the spawned binary's capabilities handshake, rather than at template registration (see `concept:host-daemon-proxy`, `concept:template`).
- `host-daemon-path-resolution-anchored-to-daemon-cwd` — The host daemon resolves each binding's path at exec time against its own working directory, without a shell, and canonicalizes it; that one resolved path serves both the allowlist match and the exec (see `concept:host-daemon`).
- `host-daemon-port-assignment-no-handshake` — The host daemon picks a free local port, tells the spawned child which port to bind, and polls that port until the child answers; the child reports no port back (see `concept:host-daemon`).
- `host-daemon-proxy-enrollment` — Under mutual-TLS service auth the host-daemon proxy enrolls with the control API through the same enrollment machinery every bundled service uses, renews its short-lived leaf automatically, and serves the supervisor-facing protocols on a listener that requires and verifies client certificates against the deployment CA — separate from the daemon-facing listener; independently of service-auth mode, the proxy's outbound control-API clients accept the same CA-bundle trust anchor bundled services read (`RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_CA`), honored whenever the control-API URL is HTTPS.
- `host-daemon-proxy-error-vocabulary-reuse` — Every host-daemon-proxy dispatch failure surfaces on the supervisor-facing protocol as an ordinary executor-error or claim-producer-unavailable terminal; the proxy adds no error class of its own (see `concept:host-daemon-proxy`, `concept:error-policy`).
- `host-daemon-proxy-tls` — Two distinct host-daemon hops, secured two ways: the daemon dials the proxy over TLS in every posture with the api-key inside the channel, and the daemon-to-child loopback runs mandatory mutual TLS from a self-contained local enrollment authority (see `concept:host-daemon`, `concept:service-auth`).
- `host-daemon-proxy-uniform-routing-identity` — Every dispatch resolves its serving daemon by the instance's stamped routing identity — an api-key id, or the assigned silly-name in anonymous mode — so the proxy carries no separate anonymous routing rule (see `concept:host-daemon-proxy`, `concept:anonymous-mode`).
- `http-bridge-preserved` — The claude-agent executor exposes an HTTP-JSON bridge (health, execute, observability routes) alongside gRPC for standalone deployments.
- `http-router-chi` — The go-chi/chi router, pinned to a stable major line — lightweight and net/http-native.
- `idempotency-key-header-universal` — A mandatory idempotency key on every message-send surface — the header on the universal endpoint, a required argument on the MCP tool — rejected when omitted and never minted for the caller (see `concept:message`, `concept:control-api`).
- `idempotency-status-code-distinction` — A created-resource status code on fresh insert versus an OK status code on replay (returning the original message identifier — see `concept:message`).
- `image-entrypoint-role-selection` — The shared entrypoint binary with no command → all roles; a single role command → that role; any other command exits non-zero naming the value; migrate runs once per deployment, owner role determined by command, synchronously before any role starts (see `concept:rimsky`).
- `image-set-bundled-services` — One image per bundled service (claim producers, sensors, subscribers, executors), so a deployment pulls only the services it runs.
- `image-set-four-core` — Four core images: a base image carrying every role binary plus the shared entrypoint, a dev-friendly all-in-one variant baked with SQLite defaults so it runs zero-config, the host-daemon proxy image, and the conformance-runner image.
- `image-tagging-version-and-channel` — An immutable per-version tag plus a mutable channel tag — one channel for formal releases and a separate channel for dev releases.
- `image-two-stage` — An Alpine-based Go toolchain image for the build stage; a distroless static base image running as a non-root user for the runtime stage.
- `implementation-language-go-plus-ts` — A single primary systems language (Go) for all core code; TypeScript exists only as a type-declaration stub for the protocols module's wire contract.
- `in-place-retry` — When the per-error-class policy chain resolves to `retry`, the supervisor loops in-process on the same node-run row across both executor and acquire surfaces; no new row is created and the row's state does not transition for retry.
- `inproc-eventstream` — A unary in-process executor call returning one Outcome, bridged through a goroutine and buffered channel solely for caller-cancellation and panic isolation — no event stream, no receive loop.
- `inproc-handler-interface` — In-process utility executors implement a small Go interface in the runtime executor package: one Execute method that takes a context, the executor's execute-request DTO, and a handler-context struct carrying the cascade-message sender; the handler returns the terminal Outcome DTO directly, or an error the shared dispatch layer translates into an error terminal.
- `inproc-registry` — An in-process registry (a map from executor identity to handler) constructed explicitly at supervisor startup.
- `inproc-transport-client` — The in-process executor client is a third transport on the executor client pool's factory alongside gRPC and HTTP-bridge, resolving handlers from the in-process registry so transport stays opaque to dispatch.
- `internal-mcp-server-net-http` — claude-agent's per-dispatch internal MCP callback server uses the standard-library HTTP stack speaking the JSON-RPC subset the CLI uses, shut down gracefully after the in-flight terminal report.
- `intx-suffix-convention` — The `...InTx` suffix on a persistence-layer function means it requires an already-open transaction passed by its caller; the retired paired-variant idiom does not return, with one method taking an optional transaction parameter as the house shape.
- `jcs-cyberphone` — A spec-compliant JCS canonicalization library.
- `keepalive-endpoint` — A dedicated keepalive route on the supervisor, keyed by run id and authenticated with the dispatch's cancel token, persisting two effects in one transaction: it bumps the dispatch's last-progress timestamp and renews the expiry of every claim the run holds.
- `kind-sugar-resolver` — Add a new optional kind field on the template node definition (alongside the existing required routing-key field, which is unchanged).
- `late-bound-services-direct-spawn` — Under the self-hosted ephemeral-run verb, late-bound service bindings reuse the compose one-shot's direct-spawn path — loopback-reached out-of-process executors, not in-proc handlers, and no separate host daemon or proxy config required.
- `launch-config-injection` — The compose verb writes one synthetic unified config file to the run directory, the supervisor's tuning under its per-role section, and points the role runners at it through the standard config-discovery surface (see `concept:rimsky-yml`).
- `launch-integration` — One exported launcher runs the three role runners — scheduler, supervisor, control-api: it starts each in order, tracks each runner's stop function, owns the combined role-failure channel, and drains in reverse order; the all-in-one entrypoint and the compose verb both call it, and each site writes its own signal-versus-failure select.
- `layer-ordering` — Within the root module, four ordered layers: the foundation module's layer → the graph layer → the runtime layer → the control layer, enforced by depguard.
- `licensing-dual-apache-agpl` — Per `concept:module-layout`, dual-track licensing across two surfaces: a permissive open-source license covers the protocols module (the surface external implementers link against); a strong-copyleft license with a commercial alternative covers the other eight code groups (the foundation module, graph layer, runtime layer, control layer, the bundled services, the binaries group, the test group, the tools group); a file outside those nine groups, such as the planner estate, carries no track.
- `licensing-enforced-by-license-lint` — Enforced by a build-step license check that constrains Apache-licensed packages to import only the standard library plus permissive-licensed and Apache-licensed dependencies (see `concept:module-layout`).
- `lifecycle-drain-per-role` — Each of the three runtime roles runs its own drain over the one lifecycle outbox and kicks it the moment it stages a row, so delivery never waits on the reconciler interval in any deployment.
- `lifecycle-fanout-after-commit` — Every lifecycle-subscriber delivery runs outside the transaction that performs the transition, which stages it as an outbox row; a subscriber's error never refuses or rolls back the transition (see `concept:lifecycle-subscriber`).
- `lifecycle-subscriber-at-least-once-delivery` — Rimsky delivers each lifecycle event at least once: the transition stages an outbox row, the drain retries a failed delivery on a widening interval, and the row is deleted in the transaction that records the acknowledgement; subscriber handlers must be idempotent (see `concept:lifecycle-subscriber`).
- `lineage-identity-hashed-not-raw` — A lineage record references identity and substrate by content hash; a held-claim reference carries the hash of the claim-scope data rather than the data itself (see `concept:lineage-record`, `concept:inertness`).
- `lineage-records-computation-only` — A leaf-run lineage record is written only at the terminal of a run that invoked an executor, under a closed family of four terminal kinds; a run that invokes no executor writes none (see `concept:lineage-record`, `concept:lineage`).
- `lineage-subscriber-poller` — The bundled lineage subscriber emits by periodically polling the durable lineage projection against a cursor rather than registering as a push-style lifecycle subscriber; polling is restart-safe and at-least-once by construction.
- `logging-slog-only` — Stdlib structured logging, written as JSON; every rimsky-authored process installs the same handler and takes its level from one shared environment variable, `RIMSKY_LOG_LEVEL`.
- `loop-counter-shape` — The loop-counter utility kind is a carry-forward counter: a required positive maximum, an executor-owned count carried forward intra-frame via the outcome's attributes delta, and step vs done tags on Success.
- `mcp-http-parity` — The MCP tool catalog is a full-parity projection of the HTTP control-api surface through the same auth and permission gates; MCP is a transport, never a second API.
- `message-idempotencies-dedup-tuple` — Per-instance, per-sender-kind, per-sender, per-sender-subject, per-idempotency-key (see `concept:message`).
- `message-queue-mode-per-instance` — Per-instance `message_queue_mode` (values `backlog` (default) or `coalesce`) declared on the template and materialized onto the instance row at creation; coalesce cancels any prior pending messages for the instance at receipt, bounding the queue at ≤ 1.
- `message-sender-kind-discriminator` — The message envelope carries three sender fields: the sender-kind discriminator `operator` / `publisher` / `instance`, the sender identity minted within that kind, and the sender-subject behind the send where one exists (see `concept:message`).
- `metrics-prometheus-client` — Metrics are exported with the standard Prometheus Go client library over a scrapeable endpoint.
- `migration-direct` — A one-shot self-hosting run migrates its freshly-created SQLite database in-process before starting any role runner; no migrate-binary subprocess.
- `migrations-append-only-numbered` — Numerically ordered, append-only, per backend (see `concept:persistence-database`), with one bounded pre-v1 baseline-collapse allowance; the runner records each applied file's digest and refuses the next boot by name when a recorded file's contents changed.
- `migrations-no-compat-shims` — Drop + recreate when cleaner; no compat shims.
- `mode-default-most-recent` — The per-template cascade-mode configuration defaults to `most-recent` (coalesce intermediate cascades), with `sequenced` and the two idempotent variants available as opt-ins for workloads that need every round or bag-dedup.
- `module-split` — Root + the foundation module + the protocols module + the services module tied by the workspace definition with local-path `replace`s.
- `mounting-subscriptions-accepted-for-message-send` — The message-send endpoint's publisher capability check accepts a subscription row in the active or the mounting state, and rejects a failed row, a stopped row, and another instance's subscription (see `concept:publisher-subscription`).
- `multi-protocol-service-distinct-handler-per-protocol` — A binary implementing several rimsky protocols implements a distinct handler per protocol and registers each separately; rimsky defines no shared capabilities-provider abstraction across protocols (see `concept:service`).
- `named-lock-metric` — The named-lock acquisition surface increments the acquisition metric family, labeled to distinguish named locks from producer claims, following the existing metric naming convention (see `story:named-lock-metric`, `concept:named-lock`, `concept:observability`).
- `network-binding` — The control-api binds loopback by default with a configuration-overridable bind address (wide bind is the sanctioned split/containerized posture); the supervisor's callback listener binds wide and requires an advertise host.
- `no-cross-frame-attribute-caching` — Every substitution, diff-gate, and cascade decision reads only attribute rows produced inside the running frame; state that must travel across frames rides message payloads, instance params, claim payloads, or threaded sub-graph inputs (see `concept:frame`).
- `no-event-substitution` — The substitution grammar has no per-emission event path; per-emission data is read through the node-attribute substitution path.
- `no-force-fresh-trigger-if-missing-flags` — The substitution grammar carries no always-re-execute flag and no lazy-upstream-initialization flag; an author uses explicit invalidation and the cascade's proactive upstream pull instead (see `concept:attribute`, `concept:cascade`).
- `no-resume-context` — The executor wire carries no dedicated resume-context channel; executor state crossing a park-and-resume rides scratch.
- `node-config-schema-format-go` — The Go claude-agent handler embeds its node-config JSON Schema as a file and validates dispatch-time writebacks against it with rimsky's own JSON-Schema library.
- `node-reset-clears-failure-marker` — The node-reset endpoint is an observability-surface verb: it clears the failed run's persisted settling-signal marker and affects dispatch eligibility in no way (retry budgets are per-dispatch).
- `node-state-retired-from-operator-api` — The operator-facing node response does not carry a single synthesized `state` field; operators read run lifecycle through the categorical per-state run summary or the per-run endpoint instead.
- `non-cascade-direct-to-stale` — Operator-invalidate, fanout-parent recalculate, and message-delivery create a new node-run directly in `stale` (skipping pending) with carry-forward bag and immune to all `cascade_mode` rules.
- `object-store-watching-model` — deposited-content watching is one sensor over pluggable object-store backends; the local filesystem is a backend, not a second sensor.
- `one-message-per-frame` — Every frame carries at most one delivered message.
- `openlineage-outbound-bearer` — The bundled OpenLineage subscriber can present an optional outbound bearer token to a secured receiver — rimsky as the client complying with a third party's auth (see `concept:service-auth`).
- `operator-env-namespaced-per-service` — New bundled-service operator env vars carry a per-service `RIMSKY_<SERVICE>_*` prefix; pre-existing generic per-executor env vars and infrastructure knobs every process reads the same way, such as the log level, stay unprefixed.
- `orphan-reaper-connection-state` — For sync dispatches, the supervisor's gRPC client failure drives in-band claim cleanup.
- `parallel-cap-removal` — No module carries a test-parallelism cap as scheduling insurance — tests wait on observable state; the one admitted cap bounds every suite that boots containers against the one docker daemon (the services module's stack suites plus the root and foundation modules' testcontainers-backed scenario and persistence suites), and any cap must name the contention it guards.
- `parallel-inproc-claim-producer-registry` — Claim producers get an in-process registry parallel to the executor one; the in-proc client enforces the same capability envelope as the gRPC service client and registration rejects inconsistent mix-in advertisement, keeping the two modes protocol-equivalent.
- `parity-expansion` — The driver-parity suite (the cross-driver test library run against both persistence drivers) covers every queue, claim-handle, and frame behavior the runtime depends on, executed against both drivers; the wrong-claimant guard suite (see `decision:guard-conformance-suite`) is one slice of it.
- `per-service-load-opts-from-env` — Each bundled service's handler package owns one env-options construction function shared by the standalone main and the in-process registration entrypoint; unconfigured is distinct from misconfigured.
- `persistence-driver` — Use the SQLite adapter of `concept:persistence-database`, pointed at a state-database artifact under the per-run artifact directory.
- `persistence-dual-backend` — Both Postgres and SQLite, selected by a driver-selector field in the unified config.
- `plumb-validation-roles` — The validation-registry dial walks every service kind and honors declared validation-supported roles identically: publishers via their capability surface, executors via the executor-observability capabilities, same as claim producers (see `story:validation-mixin-uniform`).
- `policies-service-side-enforcement` — Each bundled service enforces its own operator allowlists inside its handler code and reports rejections as executor-protocol error outcomes; rimsky never reads, validates, or acknowledges policy content.
- `polling-audit` — Test waits divide by what they wait on: a genuine outcome-wait may poll; a wait whose pass depends on an ordering assumption blocks on the event-log tail, the durable record of the transition; every wait the lint admits carries a marker naming its class.
- `post-frame-review-over-frame-blocking-park` — Rimsky offers no indefinite park — every park carries a resume-at — and its supported idiom for human review is post-frame review by a follow-on graph or instance (see `concept:parked-state`, `concept:frame`).
- `postgres-pgx-v5` — Postgres access is `jackc/pgx/v5` through its native interface repo-wide, pinned to the v5 major line, with the dependency lint denying the driver's standard-SQL adapter package everywhere; lib/pq was rejected.
- `pre-v1-break-freely` — No backwards-compat guarantee on wire / config / event-log / resource interface; delete dead code rather than carrying it forward.
- `pre-v1-pure-removal-for-retired-surfaces` — Retired DSL surfaces are removed from the code entirely.
- `prior-stale-recovery-rename` — One prior-dispatch disposition value, `PRIOR_STALE_RECOVERY` (storage form `stale_recovery`), covers both async quiet-period stale and sync RPC-broken stale without naming which detection signal fired.
- `producer-declared-classes-capability` — The claim-producer capabilities response carries a declared-error-classes field, mirroring the executor-observability declaration; the capabilities handshake stores it in the discovery cache alongside the executor vocabularies (see `concept:discovery-cache`).
- `producer-error-passthrough` — The control-api error writer recognizes producer-error types: the producer's error class and message are carried in the response body, under a status distinguishing producer rejection from rimsky internal error (see `story:producer-error-passthrough`).
- `progress-default` — Per-node lifecycle: one line per instance creation, one per node-run terminal, one per instance terminal.
- `progress-flags` — `--quiet` collapses output to the final aggregate summary; `--verbose` adds frame-tick lines; `--json` switches every line to a JSON object (JSON Lines); the flags compose.
- `project-agnostic` — No code/doc/test/example/comment names or assumes a specific consumer; templates use generic names.
- `promotion-lineage-record-after-commit` — For a claim whose producer speaks the data-processing protocol, rimsky writes the claim-terminal lineage record once, after the commit response lands, carrying the version identifier that response returns (see `concept:lineage-record`, `concept:data-processing`).
- `protocol-version-v1-namespaced` — A single v1 protocol namespace for the entire contract surface: every proto package and every control-API HTTP route — including the executor async-callback surface and the observability sub-router — sits under one v1 namespace.
- `protojson-gateway` — The HTTP gateway marshals bodies with `protojson`, the canonical proto-to-JSON mapping — no hand-maintained JSON vocabulary beside the gRPC contract.
- `proxy-single-spawn-multiplexing` — Concurrent dispatches against one (run-scope, binding-name) multiplex over the single daemon connection with per-dispatch stream identifiers; only one spawn is ever issued.
- `race-injection-hooks` — The runtime's deterministic injection-hook pattern (a post-commit hook a test can use to force a precise interleaving) extends to deterministic injection tests at the defended concurrency seams: the acquire-unavailable abandon path, the folded ownership-bail path, the held-claim aggregate check-and-fire, and the orphan-reaper vs in-flight-terminal overlap.
- `registry-hub-rimskyai-namespace` — Images publish under the hyphenless `rimskyai` namespace on Docker Hub — Hub's namespace grammar disallows the hyphenated `rimsky-ai` GitHub organization name.
- `release-attestations` — Build-tool attestations with both provenance (max mode) and SBOM enabled.
- `release-chain` — Lint → license lint → build the core images → build the bundled-service images → run the full test suite → scan the built images → push the images → read each pushed tag's published platforms back from the registry and fail on a mismatch.
- `release-dev-mechanical` — The dev-release flow is mechanical: no SemVer judgment, no notes, version derived as the next minor pre-release with a dev pre-release suffix that includes a build date and the current commit hash.
- `release-distribution` — Four channels: attested container images published as multi-platform indexes covering Linux on Intel and ARM, the protocols npm package, Go modules from a full checkout, and GitHub Releases with prebuilt CLI archives; Windows and network `go install` are named non-channels.
- `release-formal-skill` — The formal-release skill drives SemVer judgment + notes draft + outward push behind a single user gate.
- `release-notes-template` — Release notes are template-driven — a fixed section set covering breaking changes, features, fixes, internals, and each distribution channel — with every entry tracing to a diff hunk.
- `release-scan-docker-scout` — Docker Scout scans every locally-built image in the release chain, failing the release on any unaddressed critical or high finding.
- `release-semver-from-diff` — Derived from diff inspection (proto, migrations, exports, CLI flags, env vars).
- `release-semver-sha-dot-joined` — Dot-joined into the SemVer pre-release segment, not appended as build metadata.
- `revive-no-exported-rule` — Disable the lint rule that requires every exported symbol to carry a comment.
- `rimsky-compose-run-scope` — The compose one-shot verb stays manifest-only; it is not extended to accept template files, since the ephemeral-run verb covers the single-template case.
- `rimsky-run-self-hosts-templates` — The ephemeral-run verb self-hosts an all-in-one stack and drives a single template to terminal when no target endpoint is present, reusing the compose one-shot's self-host machinery.
- `run-name` — Default the run name from the compose manifest's project field.
- `run-scope-is-per-frame` — A RunScope is created inside a frame and lives for that frame's lifetime alone, rejecting a per-instance main-RunScope alternative that would let scoped properties bleed across frames.
- `run-token-swept` — The one-time terminal return leg carries no per-call token — mTLS service identity (or the trusted subnet under `none`) authenticates it, and the executor-chosen `async_ack_id` is a correlation key, never an authenticator.
- `scratch-column` — Executor scratch persists as a byte column on the node-run row, committed with the row (see `decision:attribute-bytes-in-the-row`); default is empty.
- `scratch-protocol` — Scratch rides the execute request and the three settling terminal outcomes (success, error, park) only — the transient async hand-off carries none, and an empty terminal scratch is a no-op against the row's persisted scratch, not a clear.
- `scratch-recovery` — Scratch is per-dispatch-row: the recalculate enqueue copies it forward at row creation; dead-supervisor recovery and in-place retry reuse the same row, so no copy is needed.
- `secret-at-rest-posture` — Secrets at rest are protected in graduated tiers by value: api-keys as one-way hashes, the deployment CA private key app-level encrypted, config-blob secrets delegated to operator controls, and instance params stored and returned as written (see `concept:api-key`, `concept:publisher-subscription`).
- `send-as-node-kind` — Cascade-driven message send lives on a dedicated node-kind declared by a message-send directive in place of an executor binding, and it is the only in-graph path that opens a frame.
- `sensor-emission-permanent-drop-vs-transient-retry` — A sensor permanently drops a message the control API rejects and advances its consumed state; a transient failure leaves consumed state unadvanced, so the next cycle re-attempts the observation (see `concept:sensor`).
- `sequence-scope-monotonic` — A node-run's sequence is assigned per `(node, run-scope)` as the largest existing sequence plus one; frame identity does not participate, so the latest-run lookup has a deterministic answer.
- `service-auth-mtls` — Internal service↔service auth is a two-mode deployment switch, default off: under mutual TLS a control-plane CA issues short-lived certs to services that enroll by api-key, and both services of every internal dial mutually authenticate (see `concept:service-auth`).
- `service-delivery-stall-signal` — Both service-delivery retry loops persist their failure state on the outbox row; a service whose oldest pending row has waited longer than `service_delivery.stall_after` is stalled, and rimsky writes one event-log entry at the stall and one at the next success, beside a per-outbox diagnostics route listing what each service is owed.
- `service-spawn-flag` — The compose-run verb accepts a per-service spawn flag mapping a service name to a local binary (with bare-name aliases), mirroring the standalone run verb's service-spawn flag.
- `service-tls-enforcement` — The service TLS config key is writable on executor, store, and publisher service entries, and every service dial site honors the configured mode — the runtime's service clients (store, publisher, data-processing, validation), the executor dial, and the observability-handshake dial: the required mode dials with verified TLS against system roots; the off mode (the default) stays plaintext; failures under the required mode name the service and the mode (see `story:service-tls-enforced`).
- `services-source` — The compose manifest schema carries an executors block and a claim-producers block, mirroring the corresponding blocks in `concept:rimsky-yml`.
- `signoff-crypto-ed25519` — Sign-off validation verifies an ed25519 signature over the domain-separated bound output via the standard-library primitive; the signing shape (algorithm, domain separation, RFC 8785 canonicalization) is a wire-compatibility contract held by fixed cross-implementation test vectors.
- `single-frame-creation-path` — A frame opens only when a message lands in the ledger and the next frame boundary picks it up.
- `single-process-mode` — The entrypoint's no-command path runs all three roles in one process via the library entry points with bundled handlers registered in-proc; a process-role env marker names unified mode, and the roles read it to place their metrics listeners and to decide whether the embedded-file backend needs the shared-file warning.
- `spec-jcs-canonicalization` — The template-spec hash is computed over canonical bytes produced by RFC 8785 JCS.
- `sqlite-modernc-pure-go` — SQLite persistence uses modernc.org/sqlite, a pure-Go driver requiring no CGO.
- `sqlite-multiproc-safety` — Two halves. (1) The SQLite-backed persistence driver's read-then-write operations are transactional — no bare read-then-write surfaces relying on in-process connection serialization — so immediate-mode transactions provide cross-process atomicity. (2) The SQLite-backed advisory locker's scheduler-tick and migration locks are filesystem-lock-based (lock files alongside the database file), so tick and migration exclusion hold across processes sharing the file — without this, two scheduler processes would sweep concurrently, the exact condition `decision:sweep-lock-skip-on-error` exists to prevent.
- `structural-root-edges-derived-on-demand` — The runtime derives a template's inverse-edge map on demand from the stored spec and memoizes it per template hash; the builder adds one synthetic entry per structural-root receiver, waking on a success terminal without forcing upstream refresh. The canonical template hash covers the spec bytes alone.
- `structured-log-kind-format` — Every structured process-log emit site names its kind as a raw string literal in the events standard's `SUBSYSTEM.NOUN.VERB` form, prose in a field rather than in the kind, held by a lint with an empty baseline; the event log is a different system and keeps its closed enum.
- `subclaims-as-input` — Sub-claim acquisition is owned by fan-out's partition-split mechanics (see `concept:fan-out`); the dispatch-children primitive consumes already-acquired sub-claims as input.
- `subgraph-closure-no-free-upstream-reference` — A node inside a sub-graph cannot read attributes from the calling graph's upstream nodes by free reference; calling-graph state reaches it only through the calling node's own inputs (see `concept:delegation`).
- `subscription-edges-only-from-explicit-block` — Two sources feed the subscription-edge map: the explicit subscribes block, and exactly one runtime injection added when the runtime derives the map — a structural-root edge per no-upstream main-graph node, waking on the empty-type message-receiver's settlement. Substitution refs contribute no edges.
- `subscription-mounting-state` — The publisher-subscription state set covers mounting / active / failed / stopped; instance-create inserts subscription rows in the mounting state and returns; the instance-detail surface exposes per-subscription state (see `concept:publisher-subscription`).
- `subscription-reconciler` — A reconciliation worker performs Subscribe RPCs for mounting subscription rows at a fixed interval with no attempt cap, and the startup resync pass issues only the rows missing from each publisher's live set and flips back a row that failed on a then-unregistered publisher name.
- `substitution-deps-from-persisted-senders` — The substitution-context builder enumerates the receiver's subscribed sender node types and reads each sender's most-recent fresh-settled attribute data directly from the per-run ledger; the wait-set is not consulted for sender data (wake-only).
- `substitution-failure-routes-with-substitution` — Attribute substitution failures are classified and applied to the receiver's `template_resolution_failed` error-class policy in the same transaction where substitution runs, so the sender's commit is decoupled from a receiver bag-build failure.
- `substitution-grammar-closed` — The substitution grammar is a closed enumeration of data-reference tokens plus an optional literal fallback, admitting no cascade-shape tokens and no function forms.
- `substitution-grammar-fallback-routing` — Unresolved substitution refs route through the fallback / lenient / optional handling at dispatch whenever a ref's source value is absent; a directive carries at most one literal fallback, and never both a fallback and the lenient marker.
- `substitution-per-field-arity-one-to-one` — Each substitution directive resolves against exactly one source value; several directives in one field concatenate their values and never sum them, and many-to-many fan-in lives on the cascade surface (see `concept:attribute`).
- `substitution-ref-coverage-required` — Every substitution ref in a node's attribute schema must be matched by at least one subscription entry whose sender and type would deliver the corresponding signal; registration rejects templates with uncovered refs.
- `sweep-lock-skip-on-error` — In the scheduler tick, an error from the advisory-lock attempt is treated as lock-held: log and skip the sweep pass, never run unlocked (see `concept:advisory-lock`).
- `synthetic-envelope-mechanism-retired` — Receivers wake exclusively via the subscriber-side cascade walker; no synthetic-envelope chokepoint, runtime-internal type-paths, or wake-node-id wire fields exist.
- `tag-based-subscription` — The signal taxonomy carries no `event/<name>` leaf; named-event subscription is `terminal/*` plus a CEL `when:` filter over the terminal payload's tag set.
- `template-identity-deployment-canonical` — A template's identity is the content hash of its spec after the deployment's canonicalization, which reads the deployment's kind-alias map; a client obtains the hash from the deployment rather than computing it (see `concept:template`).
- `template-registration-validation-unconditional` — Template registration validates every executor, store, and named-lock reference and requires each declared executor's expected-attributes schema to be visible and satisfied; only the spec's own late-bind list exempts a service (see `concept:template`).
- `terminal-error-abandoned-as-error-class` — The held-claim abandon outcome cascades as `terminal/error/abandoned`, slotting into the existing `terminal/error/<class>` taxonomy rather than introducing a new top-level signal root.
- `terminal-tags` — Executor terminals carry set-semantics `tags`; no named-event message or streaming named-event variant exists, and `declared_tags` advertises the emit vocabulary.
- `termination` — The run-to-terminal verbs own termination: each polls the instances it created until every one is quiescent — no running frame, no pending message — then terminates each and exits (see `concept:instance`).
- `test-harness-create-instance-wakes-roots-after-create` — The scenario test harness's create-instance helpers gain an internal empty-message wake step after the create POST so existing wait-for-root-dispatch semantics still hold without per-test changes.
- `test-harness-invalidate-node-retired` — The scenario test harness's invalidate-node helper retires entirely (both branches).
- `test-wallclock-lint-ratchet` — Wall-clock verdict idioms in test code are lint-forbidden — fail-on-timeout selects, deadline-bounded poll loops, deadline-polling helpers, a context deadline whose expiry feeds a verdict, and a test that writes a package-level variable: the gate fails on any violation, the recorded baseline is empty, every wait the lint admits carries a class marker, and a per-site suppression for a sleep that is not a verdict input carries its justification.
- `testcontainers-go` — An integration-test container helper that boots real container instances of the persistence backends from inside the Go test process.
- `testing-scenario-based-e2e` — End-to-end via the test group's scenarios directory + the services module's scenarios test directory driving the assembled product; persistence tests use an integration-test container helper to boot real backends. Harness wait helpers are poll-until-success: they block until the awaited state appears, and they report the expected-versus-observed state descriptively when the run is cut short. The suites run with no per-package time ceiling; hang detection lives in the test guard, which watches the runner's event stream and kills a run only when no test has completed for a long interval.
- `three-dispatch-deadlines` — Three independent per-node deadlines govern each dispatch (sync RPC bound, async quiet-period, absolute runtime), with `0` as the disable sentinel and no executor-level deadline layer beneath them.
- `timeout-flag` — The run-to-terminal verbs' wall-clock timeout is opt-in with no default; absence means "as long as it takes."
- `timestamp-format` — ISO 8601 UTC with colons replaced by hyphens: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ`.
- `tls-mode-validation` — The service TLS config field is parse-time validated, accepting exactly off-or-required; an empty field inherits the deployment's service-auth posture — off while service auth is unset or none, required once service auth is mutual TLS — and opportunistic or any other value is a config error.
- `toplevel-dirs` — The cmd group, the lib group, the test group, the tools group.
- `topology-test-coverage` — The services integration harness carries a standing proof for each supported deployment shape — the single-process all-in-one and the three-container split — each booting the real topology and driving the same scenario to terminal.
- `uncovered-substitution-error-shape` — Registration rejection for an uncovered substitution ref returns a structured `validation_errors` entry, kind-discriminated, identifying the offending ref and carrying a copy-pasteable drop-in subscription-entry suggestion plus a separate note explaining the refresh flag's implications.
- `uniform-attributes-delta` — Only the run-terminating verdicts (`terminal/success`, `terminal/error/<class>`) carry `attributes_delta`, committed atomically with the verdict and exposed on the signal payload for CEL predicates; park carries none, and the coexisting mid-dispatch writeback callback emits no signal.
- `upstream-gating-at-eligibility` — The dispatch-eligibility predicate carries the propagation-path-independent condition: a stale run is not eligible while any subscribed upstream has an in-flight run in the same frame.
- `validation-errors-additive-not-uniform` — Validation-error responses are an array of entries that may be of two shapes: a `{path, msg}` entry for simple field violations, and a structured entry carrying a `kind` discriminator plus additional fields for violations that the operator (or an LLM agent) needs to act on programmatically.
- `validator-learns-producer-classes` — The template validator range-checks the node's error-type policy keys against the union of the executor's declared classes, the synthetic acquire-side error family, and the declared error classes (see `decision:producer-declared-classes-capability`) of every producer reachable from the node's claims.
- `wait-set-topic-kind-taxonomy` — 4-value taxonomy: three canonical kinds (`terminal`, `transient`, `attribute`) projecting the signal taxonomy plus `state` as a defensive fallback for rows whose pattern does not map to a canonical kind.
- `walker-rule-per-sender-node` — The cascade walker accumulates a new wait-set row into the latest cascade-driven pending iff the sender's node is not already in that pending's sender-nodes set; a repeat from the same sender-node creates a new pending.
- `webhook-auth-required` — The bundled webhook sensor requires per-subscription auth — one of `hmac`, `secret_header`, or an explicit `none` — refused fail-loud at bind time when the `auth` block is absent (see `concept:sensor`, `concept:service-auth`).
- `wire-commit-response-fields` — The producer client returns the base Commit response body; the unified claim-handle resolution engine persists `version_id` from the base Commit response to the claim-handle row; the settle-children path surfaces `producer_metadata` in the fan-out parent's writeback — as the claim-producer protocol's documentation promises (see `story:commit-response-honored`, `concept:child-execution`).
- `write-semantics-reader-lease-forbidden` — A producer advertising staged-asynchronous write semantics serves readers a point-in-time snapshot; serializing readers behind an internal lease is not support for that value (see `concept:write-semantics`).
- `write-semantics-three-level-structure` — Write-semantics support is pinned at three levels: the producer's advertised set, the operator's narrowing set per producer, and the one realized value each open verb returns (see `concept:write-semantics`).
- `writeback-bumps-progress` — Each mid-dispatch attribute writeback callback updates the dispatch row's progress timestamp in the same transaction as the attribute write; a genuine writeback is itself a liveness signal (see `concept:supervisor`, `decision:keepalive-endpoint`).
